summary: Answer every call in under a minute, lead paid budget with water heater replacement, and pre-load spend before the first hard freeze. Use with the Miles Master Template (deploy logic, ZIP scoring, customer journey).

sections.title: Intro
lines: Answer every call in under a minute, lead paid budget with water heater replacement, and pre-load spend before the first hard freeze. Use with the Miles Master Template (deploy logic, ZIP scoring, customer journey).

sections.title: 1. At a glance
lines: Mostly emergency (leaks, clogs, no hot water); some planned (repipes, water treatment)
Water heater replacement (highest margin to lead with)
Cost per lead to hold against
Tank water heaters last about 8–12 years; tankless up to ~20

sections.title: 2. Seasonality by region
lines: Plumbing has no clean season; the hooks are freeze events, holidays, and equipment age.
Dec–Feb freezes; spring thaw sump and flooding
Pre-freeze pipe protection Oct–Nov; burst-pipe emergency Dec–Feb
First hard freeze; Thanksgiving to New Year drain load
Pre-load budget before the first freeze forecast
Rare freezes hit hardest (pipes unprotected); storm flooding
Freeze-event surge campaigns; slab leaks; hurricane season sump/backflow
Holiday spike: Thanksgiving through New Year (kitchen drains, guests, garbage disposals) in every region.

sections.title: 3. Location signals (add to ZIP score)
lines: Median year built: pre-1980 housing means galvanized or cast iron pipes (repipe and sewer-line candidates); 8–12-year-old housing means first water heater replacement.
Freeze days per year and how rare freezes are (rare-freeze ZIPs surge hardest).
Slab vs basement foundations (slab-leak vs sump/backflow demand).

sections.title: 4. Demographics and audiences
lines: Emergency buyer: anyone with a leak; searches "plumber near me" and calls the first answered number with good reviews.
Planned buyer: homeowner 35–70 replacing a water heater, softener, or repiping; compares price and warranty.
Landlords and property managers: recurring work, volume pricing.
Audiences: past customers by water heater install date; homeowners in older-housing ZIPs; retargeting to estimates.

Load with the Audience framework in the Master Template. Emergency segments get no income or homeowner filter and start at 25+; planned segments use the filters below. Ages are starting points: Miles tightens them from closed-won CRM data after 30 booked jobs.
LSA + Search carry 85% of budget; no demographic exclusions
median year built 8-15+ yrs ago; owner-occupied >= 60%
Search: water heater terms; observe Homeowners
customers with water heater install date 8+ yrs ago
Search: repipe, sewer camera, sewer line replacement
Search: commercial plumber, property management plumbing
Exclude in every segment: customers from the last 12 months (except retention campaigns), open leads and estimates, employees, out-of-area ZIPs.

sections.title: 5. Offer stack
lines: $[X] diagnostic credited to repair, or waived dispatch fee with qualifying repair
$[X] off water heater replacement, installed in 24 hrs
Tankless, softener / filtration, whole-home repipe, sewer camera inspection
Annual plumbing check: water heater flush, drain and fixture check, priority service
Water heater age reminders; second-service credit
24/7, plumber at your door in [60] minutes, no overtime fee; never discount

sections.title: 6. Channels and campaign build
lines: LSA and Search carry 85% of budget; split emergency ("burst pipe", "leak", "clogged"), water heater, sewer/drain, and planned work.
Negatives: jobs, plumbing school, DIY, parts, "how to", supply houses.
Missed-call text-back and after-hours answering are mandatory before launch; unanswered LSA leads are the biggest waste.
Meta: water heater age and freeze-prep creative to past customers and scored ZIPs.

sections.title: 7. Triggers Miles watches
lines: Forecast ≤ 20°F, or first freeze of the season
Pre-freeze SMS to past customers; raise emergency budget 48 hrs out
Surge burst-pipe campaign; extend hours if capacity allows
Sump pump, backflow, sewer backup campaign

sections.title: 8. After the job and retention
lines: Record water heater brand, size, install date in CRM on every visit.
Thank-you coupon toward drain cleaning or next service; honest review ask to everyone.
Plumbing reactivation email: "Your water heater is [X] years old. Most tanks last 8 to 12."

sections.title: 9. Compliance and watch-outs
lines: "Free" only if truly free; diagnostic credits must state terms.
Don't promise arrival times you can't meet; speed is the brand.
Water treatment health claims need proof; keep claims to taste, scale, and appliance life.

sections.title: 10. Deploy checklist
lines: ☐ Score ZIPs with housing age and freeze profile
☐ Load water heater, emergency promise, and membership offers
☐ Build LSA + Search by service; water heater landing page
☐ Import past customers with water heater dates; arm freeze and holiday triggers
☐ Turn on missed-call text-back, speed-to-lead, post-job and reactivation automations
Sources: water heater lifespan (Angi) · tankless lifespan (Bob Vila) · CPL, budget split and leak from the Miles plumbing playbook.
